newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian ships off Sierra Leone fire, shots in city.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian ships off Sierra Leone fire, shots in city.

text.p: Nigerian naval vessels off Sierra Leone's capital fired on Monday and shooting broke out on land after negotiations with coup leaders to restore the ousted civilian president ran into trouble.

Small arms fire broke out around a beachside hotel protected by Nigerian troops where about 1,000 West African foreigners are sheltering. Security staff advised guests to move to the rooftop for safety.
Hundreds of Sierra Leoneans waving green leaves and chanting "we want peace" marched along the road outside.
Nigerian troops took up defensive positions as a helicopter left the seafront military headquarters housing the coup leaders. There was no indication who was aboard.
Nigeria, Ghana and Guinea sent troops to Sierra Leone after the May 25 coup, ready for a strike if talks with Major Johnny Paul Koromah and his Armed Forces Revolutionary Council failed.
The booming of naval guns shook the capital at 6 a.m. (0600 GMT) as Nigerian vessels opened fire. "The attack has started," said a West African military official in the capital.
A spokesman for the coup soldiers tried to reassure the population in a radio announcement.

"The bombardment that you are hearing is just to scare away people," he said, adding that a planned demonstration in the city by Sierra Leoneans and foreigners opposed to intervention would go ahead as planned later on Monday.

A Nigerian diplomat said the attack followed a breakdown of last-minute negotiations which went on late into Sunday night. "Each time we reached an agreeemnt, the chairman was nowhere to be found to sign it," he said.

The attack followed a Sunday radio broadcast in which Koromah announced his 20-member council, with rebel leader Foday Sankoh as vice chairman and including three more members of Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front (RUF).

Koromah was the highest ranked of the original coup leaders but his policy-making body includes three brigadiers and four colonels, plus a few civilians, including the secretary-general of the government and the attorney-general.
Nigerian troops in Sierra Leone came under fire from rebels on Sunday on the highway into the capital from Hastings airport to the east of town. No one was hurt.
British High Commissioner Peter Penfold and Nigerian High Commissioner Chidi Abubakar had hosted secret preliminary talks culminating in a comprehensive meeting on Sunday.
A Sierra Leonean negotiator said Penfold and Abubakar had attended talks late on Sunday at the military headquarters. "It was not a disaster but not the success that everyone had expected," he said.
A senior diplomat said Sankoh's rebels, who have been fighting a bush war since 1991 and have allied with the coupmakers, opposed a settlement and had not been in the talks.

Diplomats said the RUF's resistance to a deal had led to serious rifts between its commanders and the coup leaders. Sierra Leonean sources said two people had been killed in gunfights between RUF rebels and soldiers inside Koromah's military headquarters on a Freetown beachfront.

On Sunday U.S. helicopters evacuated the last Americans and Europeans who had taken refuge in two beachside hotels from the violence which followed the coup. Britain chartered a DC10 that arrived in London from the Guinean capital Conakry with some 230 British evacuees.
